plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the logistic sigmoid function sig[z] plotted as a single smooth curve over the range z ∈ [−5, 5]. The horizontal axis is labeled z with tick marks at −5.0, 0.0, and 5.0, and the vertical axis is labeled sig[z] with tick marks at 0.0 and 1.0. A smooth orange S-shaped curve rises monotonically from near zero on the left to near one on the right, with its steepest slope occurring at z = 0 where the function equals exactly 0.5. Gray dashed lines indicate the horizontal asymptote at sig[z] = 1.0 and mark a vertical reference at z = 0, emphasizing the function’s symmetry and its asymptotic approach to both bounds. This figure introduces the logistic sigmoid as a differentiable, bounded activation function that squashes any real-valued input into the interval (0, 1), motivating its use for modeling probabilities in binary classification.

interactionPlan.concept: The logistic sigmoid smoothly and monotonically squashes any real input z into the open interval (0,1), and its inverse (the logit) maps a chosen probability threshold back to a single z value, with the symmetric midpoint 0.5 landing exactly at z=0.
elements: horizontal axis labeled z with tick marks at -5.0, 0.0, 5.0
vertical axis labeled sig[z] with tick marks at 0.0 and 1.0
smooth orange S-shaped sigmoid curve rising from ~0 at z=-5 to ~1 at z=5, steepest at z=0
formula annotation 1 / (1 + exp[-z]) in serif math near the top-center
gray dashed vertical reference line at z = 0
gray dashed horizontal reference line at sig[z] = 0.5 meeting the vertical line at the inflection point (0, 0.5)
draggable marker point constrained to the sigmoid curve with a coordinate readout (z, sig[z])
horizontal threshold line (contrasting color) at the chosen probability with a marked intersection dot on the curve and a vertical drop to the z-axis labeling the corresponding logit z value

interactions.teaches: Reading (z, sig[z]) directly off the curve shows the forward mapping: small |z| changes the output most near the center, while the tails saturate so that large positive z stays near 1 and large negative z stays near 0

interactions.label: Probability threshold
interactions.teaches: A probability threshold corresponds to exactly one z (the log-odds / logit); sweeping it reveals the inverse mapping and that the symmetric decision threshold 0.5 sits precisely at z=0, while thresholds near 0 or 1 push the intercept far into the saturated tails

demo_steps.title: The squash
demo_steps.narration: The orange curve is sig[z] = 1/(1+exp[-z]): it maps every real z into (0,1), rising monotonically with its steepest slope at the inflection point (0, 0.5) marked by the dashed crosshairs.

demo_steps.title: Trace the curve
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker along the curve and watch the (z, sig[z]) readout: near z=0 the output moves quickly, but out in the tails it barely changes — the function saturates toward its 0 and 1 asymptotes.

demo_steps.title: Threshold to logit
demo_steps.narration: Move the probability-threshold slider: a horizontal line crosses the curve at one point and drops to the z-axis, showing the unique z (log-odds) that yields that probability. At 0.5 the intercept is exactly z=0; near 0.9 or 0.1 it shifts asymmetrically into the tails.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The sigmoid is a smooth monotonic squash from the reals to (0,1), and inverting it turns any probability threshold into a single linear decision value in z — with the natural 0.5 boundary sitting exactly at z=0 by symmetry.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: White plot area with solid black axes; thick warm-orange sigmoid curve spanning z in [-5,5]. Serif math formula 1/(1+exp[-z]) placed upper-center. Light-gray dashed vertical line at z=0 and dashed horizontal line at sig[z]=0.5 intersecting at the inflection point. The draggable trace marker is a filled dot on the curve with a small live label showing (z, sig[z]) to two decimals. The threshold interaction draws a horizontal line in a clearly distinct color (e.g. blue) at the slider's probability, a highlighted intersection dot on the curve, and a thin vertical drop to the z-axis annotated with the corresponding z (logit) value. Keep the orange curve visually dominant; reference and threshold lines thinner and lighter so the S-shape reads first.

discrepancies: The default (step-0) view is not a clean drop-in replacement for the static source: it overlays a solid blue threshold line, a blue intersection dot, an orange draggable marker with a '(z, sig[z]) = (1.50, 0.82)' readout, and a blue 'z = 0.00' axis label, none of which appear in the source image.

The gray reference crosshairs are drawn as a full-width horizontal dashed line and a full-height vertical dashed line, whereas the source shows only partial dotted segments (horizontal from the y-axis to the inflection point, and vertical from the inflection point down to the z-axis).

At the default threshold of 0.50 the solid blue threshold line is drawn exactly on top of the gray dashed y=0.5 reference line, producing a doubled/overlapping horizontal line at the inflection height.
evaluation.notes: The sigmoid curve, axis ranges, tick labels, black box, and the 1/(1+exp[-z]) fraction are faithfully reproduced in the correct orange/serif style, and the threshold-slider, draggable-trace, and 3-step demo interactions are functional and conceptually correct; the main weakness is that the default state clutters the clean source with a blue threshold line/dot, an orange marker and readout, and uses full crosshairs instead of the source's partial dotted reference lines.
action_items: Make the step-0 default state hide the blue threshold line, blue intersection dot, orange trace marker, and the '(z, sig[z])' / 'z = ...' readouts so the initial render matches the clean source figure; introduce those overlays only in the later demo steps.

Render the gray reference as two partial dotted segments (y-axis to (0,0.5) horizontally, and (0,0.5) down to the z-axis vertically) rather than full-width/full-height dashed crosshairs, to match the source.
When the threshold equals 0.5, suppress or offset the solid blue horizontal line so it does not sit directly on top of the gray y=0.5 reference line.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactivity are correct (concept_accuracy 5, no failure modes), but the generator needs concrete implementation fixes: hiding overlays in the default state, rendering partial crosshair segments instead of full lines, and handling the threshold-line overlap at 0.5.

discrepancies: At the default (step 1) state the 'Probability threshold' slider and the 'Drag the orange dot along the curve' hint are both visible but inert — the slider only draws the blue logit line from step 3 and the draggable marker only appears from step 2, so a user interacting with the default view sees no response

evaluation.notes: The default state is a near-exact drop-in for the source (orange sigmoid, black box, -5/0/5 and 0/1 ticks, rotated sig[z] and z titles, the 1/(1+exp[-z]) fraction, and the gray dotted reference lines meeting at the (0,0.5) inflection point), and the step player, threshold-to-logit slider, and draggable trace marker are all conceptually correct and functional; the main weakness is that the slider and drag hint are shown but do nothing until later steps, which muddies the default view.
action_items: Gate or visually disable the threshold slider and the 'drag the orange dot' hint until their respective steps are active (e.g., grey them out at step 1) so the default state does not advertise non-functional controls.
Optionally draw a faint always-on preview of the threshold horizontal line at the current slider value (even at step 1) so the slider gives immediate visual feedback rather than appearing dead.
Nudge the formula fraction slightly left/up if needed so it never risks touching the rising right shoulder of the curve at narrower viewports.
